AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

What this package is

cnvs is a small R graphics device, written for learning purposes: it renders base/grid graphics as JavaScript CanvasRenderingContext2D calls embedded in a standalone HTML file. The point is to have a from-scratch, heavily commented implementation that someone unfamiliar with R’s graphics engine internals can read end to end alongside R’s own R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h and R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h.

This shapes priorities differently than a normal package:

  • This is not, and will not be submitted to, CRAN. There is no cran-comments.md, no CRAN-SUBMISSION, no need to track CRAN policy compliance beyond what R CMD check already enforces for free.
  • This is not trying to be feature-complete or production quality. See the archived canvas package or webr::canvas() for a “real” canvas device. cnvs deliberately leaves things unimplemented (raster images, arbitrary clip paths, exact font metrics – see below) rather than chasing parity with them.
  • Clarity of comments is the primary code-quality bar – above brevity, above performance, above covering every edge case. A change that makes the implementation faster or shorter but harder to follow for a reader who doesn’t already know how graphics devices work is a net loss for this package, even if it would be a clear win elsewhere. See “The commenting bar” below.

Repository layout

R/
  cnvs.R            # the user-facing cnvs() device constructor
  cnvs-package.R    # package-level doc, @useDynLib tag

src/
  cnvs.h            # shared struct + declarations; a map of the whole device
  device.c          # device lifecycle: create, close, newPage, size,
                     # registering callbacks with the graphics engine --
                     # start here to understand how a device plugs into R
  draw.c            # drawing callbacks: line, rect, circle, polyline,
                     # polygon, text, clip, strWidth, metricInfo
  style.c           # R colour ints / line styles / fonts -> CSS/JS text
  write.c           # the HTML/JS text templates everything else writes into
  init.c            # native routine registration (R_init_cnvs)

tests/testthat/     # testthat edition 3
tmp/                # scratch scripts (gitignored) -- not part of the package

No vignettes, no NEWS.md, no pkgdown-only vignettes/articles/ split – the package is small enough that the README and the source comments are the documentation.

Architecture, in brief

  • One cnvs(file, width, height, pointsize, bg) call opens one FILE* and writes a self-contained .html file as drawing happens, rather than buffering in memory. Each device page (each call to the newPage callback – i.e. each top-level plot()/print() of a grid object, not each panel of a par(mfrow = ...) layout) gets its own <canvas> + <script> block.
  • The device coordinate system is set up the same way a bitmap/screen device would be (origin top-left, y increasing downward, one device unit = one CSS pixel), so coordinates arriving in callbacks can be written straight into canvas calls with no flipping.
  • Deliberately unimplemented, with the reasoning given inline next to dd->path = NULL; etc. in src/device.c: path, raster, cap, locator. Text metrics (strWidth/metricInfo) are a documented heuristic (average glyph width as a fraction of font size), not a measurement, because there is no portable way to get real font metrics without an actual rendering engine.
  • Only one rectangular clip region is tracked at a time (clip_active in cnvs_state); a new clip() call always restores any previous clip before applying the next one.

A load-bearing lesson: deviceVersion and the “definitions” callbacks

This bit a real debugging session and is easy to reintroduce, so it gets its own section rather than just a code comment.

dd->deviceVersion tells the graphics engine which bundle of optional feature groups (see the version history comment at the top of R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h) the device’s callback table actually has slots for. The group added at version 13 (R_GE_definitions) – setPattern/releasePattern/setClipPath/releaseClipPath/setMask/ releaseMask – is not optional in practice once a device claims that version or higher: grid calls dd->setMask unconditionally on every grid.newpage() (to clear any active mask), with no NULL check first. A device that claims deviceVersion = R_GE_version (the newest level) while leaving those six callbacks NULL will segfault R the first time grid-based graphics (ggplot2, lattice) draws a page – while looking completely fine under base graphics (plot(), etc.), since base graphics never triggers that code path. This is exactly what happened here (see the git history around the deviceVersion field in src/device.c).

The fix, and the pattern to keep following: dd->deviceVersion must match what’s genuinely wired up in cnvs_setup_callbacks(), not the newest API version the headers define. Currently that’s R_GE_definitions (13): the six callbacks above are implemented as explicit, commented stub functions that decline support (return R_NilValue / do nothing), and deviceVersion is set to 13 to match. Never raise deviceVersion without also implementing every callback in every version group up to and including the new value – even if the implementation is just “decline this feature”. Before considering any device change complete, exercise it through both a base-graphics plot and a grid-based one (e.g. a minimal ggplot2::ggplot(...) + geom_point()) – see the add-device-callback skill for the full checklist.

The commenting bar

Every callback and helper in src/ should be readable by someone who knows C and knows what a line chart is, but has never seen R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h before. Concretely, that means:

  • Say why, not just what. ctx->clip_active being restored before a new clip is applied is obvious from the code; why (canvas clip regions can only ever be intersected, never grown, without a restore) is the part worth a comment.
  • When a field, constant, or calling convention comes from R’s graphics engine rather than from this package’s own design, say so and point at where it’s documented (R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h, R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h, or a specific macro name) rather than asserting it as if it were an arbitrary implementation choice.
  • Flag approximations and limitations where they live, not just in the README – e.g. cnvs_StrWidth()’s heuristic explains in its own comment why an exact answer isn’t possible here, rather than silently returning a number that looks authoritative.
  • New top-level functions get a short header comment explaining what triggers the call and what it’s responsible for, matching the style already in draw.c/device.c/style.c/write.c.

This bar applies to C and R code alike. It’s fine – expected, even – for comments here to be longer relative to the code than they would be in a normal package.

Skills

When adding a new device callback (implementing raster, path, groups, or anything else currently left as a stub or NULL), load the add-device-callback skill first. It has a step-by-step recipe covering where to add the declaration/implementation/wiring, the deviceVersion trap above, and how to verify a change against both base and grid graphics before calling it done.

Development workflow

  • Document with roxygen2 (devtools::document()); markdown roxygen is enabled.
  • Run tests with devtools::test(); full checks with devtools::check(). The package should check cleanly (0 errors/warnings/notes) even though it isn’t CRAN-bound – a clean check is still the cheapest available signal that nothing is obviously broken.
  • Rebuilding compiled code: devtools::load_all() recompiles automatically; use pkgbuild::compile_dll(force = TRUE) if a change doesn’t seem to be picked up.
  • Visual verification matters more than usual for this package, since the whole point is the rendered output: after a drawing-related change, actually render the generated .html (e.g. headless Chromium – chromium-browser --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --screenshot=out.png file://... – writing the screenshot under $HOME rather than /tmp, since a snap-packaged Chromium’s /tmp is a private mount and writes there won’t show up outside it) rather than just inspecting the generated JS text.
  • tests/testthat/test-cnvs.R mixes base-graphics and skip_if_not_installed("ggplot2")-gated grid-graphics tests deliberately – keep both kinds when adding coverage for a new callback, per the lesson above.

Conventions

  • UK spelling throughout code comments, roxygen documentation, and prose (colour, organised, behaviour) – matches Language: en-GB in DESCRIPTION and the existing source.
  • Use the base R pipe (|>), not the magrittr pipe, in any R code.
  • C code targets plain C against R’s public headers (no Rcpp/cpp11) – intentional, since hiding the callback-table mechanics behind another layer of abstraction would undercut the point of the package.
  • Internal C helpers are prefixed cnvs_ (matching the one exported R function, cnvs()), UpperCamelCase after the prefix for graphics engine callbacks (cnvs_Line, cnvs_NewPage) to mirror the Device_Foo naming convention used in R’s own device sources, and lower_snake_case for ordinary helpers (cnvs_colour_to_css, cnvs_set_line_style).
